transcript: Hello, this is the Connect team. In our previous video, we showed you how to create shoes using shoe lasts. This time, we'll guide you through the process of completing shoes using the newly released shoe outsoles. The outsole is the bottom part of the shoe that touches the ground when worn. It plays a key role in both comfort and the overall look of the design. The new outsoles are available for both men and women. The men's collection includes six flat-style outsoles, while the women's collection offers nine flat-style and four heel-style outsoles, totaling 13 unique options. These outsoles are designed to attach directly to shoe uppers you've created with the shoe lasts, helping you achieve a more realistic and structured, final result. You can download the outsoles from the Connect tab in Clothes Library, or from the link in the video description. For details on how to build and register the outsoles, please visit the link in the video description. For details on how to build and register the final shoes as accessories, please refer to the tutorial video, linked below. Now let's get started and create sneakers, heels, and heel drop shoes using the new shoe outsoles. Let's take a quick look at how to download the shoe outsole from Connect and what's included in the file. First, you can access Shoe Outsoles directly through Clothes Library. Go to the Trim category, then click the Connect Asset tab. From there, use the search bar to find and instantly download the outsole you need. You can also download the file locally from Connect. After unzipping the folder, simply drag and drop it into Clothes to start using it. The downloaded zip file contains two key files, a shoe outsole trim file, and a project file with an outsole avatar and pre-drawn 3D penlines. If you're using the penline version, just open the project file inside the folder. We'll show you how to work with it in the next part of this tutorial. Now let's load the shoe outsole trim file into the upper shoe project we previously created using a shoe last. You can drag and drop the outsole trim file into an empty space in the 3D window, either from the Clothes Library or from a local folder where it was downloaded. Once loaded, the outsole will automatically appear in the same position as the shoe last, aligned to the ground. By default, the outsole is positioned on the left side. So if your upper was created on the right side, you'll need to use the Mirror Paste function to flip the upper accordingly. To do this, select all upper patterns, right-click on them in either the 3D or 2D window, and choose Copy. Then, right-click on an empty area in the window, and select Mirror Paste. Typically, outsole patterns are created based on the last shape. However, since this outsole features a heel drop structure with a sloped and uneven bottom, a slightly different approach is required. A heel drop structure is thicker at the heel than at the forefoot, which means that creating the outsole based on the last may result in a mismatch with the actual heel. So, in this workflow, we'll create the outsole pattern directly from the outsole file and then connect the upper patterns accordingly. By doing this, we can generate an accurate outsole pattern that matches the actual 3D shape and naturally reflects the unique silhouette of the heel drop design. Now, let's take a look at how to import the outsole project file into Calo and extract the outsole pattern. First, purchase the Chunky Boots outsole item from Connect. Download the purchased outsole file locally and save it. The downloaded file will be provided as a compressed folder. Inside the folder, you'll find two files. A shoe outsole trim file. A project file containing the 3D pen line drawn on the outsole OBJ, imported as an avatar file. To easily create an outsole pattern for the sloped heel drop structure, we'll use the avatar file that already includes the 3D pen line. After extracting the zip file, load the avatar file from the folder. You'll see that a 3D pen line has already been drawn to match the actual outsole shape, making it ready for pattern extraction. Click on the Flatten tool, then select the area where the 3D pen line is drawn and press Enter on the keyboard to generate the outsole pattern. Once the outsole pattern is created, change its particle distance to 5 and set the collision thickness to 1. Then, use the gizmo in the 3D window to position the pattern. You can also adjust the pattern as close as possible to the outsole for proper alignment with the upper pattern. Finally, freeze the pattern. Now, let's load the file created using the shoe last and apply the heel drop outsole. With other outsole types, we usually don't need to simulate after attaching the upper pattern and trim. However, for a heel drop outsole, simulation is necessary to properly fit the upper to the sloped sole. So we'll use the project file that contains both the upper pattern and the outsole. For details on creating the upper pattern, please refer to the shoe last tutorial. After adding the upper pattern and shoe last, they will be positioned based on the ground and overlap with the outsole. Next, delete the sole pattern from the upper pattern you created earlier. Select both the last and the upper pattern and use the gizmo to reposition them so they don't intersect with the outsole and can simulate properly. Since the previously imported outsole avatar file was only used to extract the sole pattern, you can now delete it before continuing. Then, sew the flattened sole pattern extracted from the 3D pen line to the upper pattern in the correct position. Finally, select all upper patterns. Apply the strengthen function to prevent distortion and run the simulation. You'll see that the upper pattern simulates smoothly, conforming to the shape of the heel drop outsole. Now that the upper pattern has been simulated to match the heel drop outsole shape, let's import the outsole as a trim and attach it to the upper pattern. Heel drop style shoes also require a dummy pattern for stable simulation with the garment. For detailed instructions on creating a dummy, please refer to the shoe making tutorial video linked in the description. Once the dummy has been applied and the simulation is complete, save the shoe as a Zax file using the same method as shown in the sneakers workflow. Next, let's show the outsole. The outsole which is not in the same position as the foot is placed on the outer rim of the shoe. The heel drop outsole cannot slide on the outside of the shoe. If the heel drop outsole is not in the same position, the shoe is unable to be hooked. Then, load the saved shoe and apply it to the avatar to finish. This concludes the guide on how to create shoes using three different types of outsole. Use the provided outsole files to create a variety of custom footwear designs. Thank you for watching and see you in the next video.
markdown_content: # Applying Outsoles in Clo (Sneakers, Heels & Heel Drop) This document explains how to apply different types of shoe outsoles in Clo 3D software, covering sneakers, heels, and heel drop outsoles. It details downloading outsole assets, attaching them to shoe uppers, using the Glue function, adjusting fit with gizmo tools, creating dummies for simulation, and registering finished shoes as Clo accessories. --- ## Overview of Shoe Outsoles in Clo This section covers the types of outsoles available in Clo, their role in shoe design, and how to access and prepare them for use. - **Outsoles** are the bottom parts of shoes that touch the ground, critical for comfort and aesthetics. - Clo offers **men's and women's outsole collections**: - Men: 6 flat-style outsoles - Women: 9 flat-style + 4 heel-style outsoles (total 13) - Outsoles attach directly to shoe uppers created with shoe lasts for realistic, structured shoe models. - Outsoles can be downloaded from the **Connect tab in Clothes Library** or via provided links. - Downloaded files include: - A **shoe outsole trim file** - A **project file** with an outsole avatar and pre-drawn 3D pen lines (for pattern extraction) --- ## Downloading and Loading Outsoles This section explains how to find, download, import, and initially position outsole files within Clo. - Access outsoles via Clothes Library → Trim category → Connect Asset tab → search and download. - Alternatively, download zip files locally and unzip. - Import outsole trim files by dragging them into the empty 3D window space. - The outsole auto-aligns to the ground, positioned on the left foot by default. - If your upper is on the right foot, use **Mirror Paste** to flip upper patterns: 1. Select all upper patterns. 2. Right-click → Copy. 3. Right-click empty area → Mirror Paste. - The outsole and upper are separate until attached. --- ## Attaching Outsoles to Shoe Uppers Using Glue This section details the Glue function essential for bonding outsole trims to upper patterns to ensure proper registration as a shoe accessory. - Without Glue, the outsole trim will not be included when registering the shoe. - Steps to attach outsole: 1. Press **0** to switch to bottom view. 2. Select the outsole in the 3D window to show the gizmo. 3. Click the third icon (Glue Mode) on the gizmo toolbar. 4. Hover over the upper pattern; a preview shows how outsole will attach. 5. Click the upper pattern to glue the outsole. - Use the gizmo to fine-tune outsole position and rotation. - Adjust upper height by selecting all patterns and moving them along the Y-axis with the gizmo. --- ## Creating a Dummy for Stable Simulation This section summarizes the dummy creation process to stabilize simulation when registering the shoe. - Import a saved dummy pattern file (see shoe last tutorial for details). - Adjust dummy position to match shoe. - Delete the dummy’s insole pattern and sew the dummy to the shoe upper’s insole. - Ensure upper fits entirely within the dummy to avoid sticking out during simulation. - Set dummy fabric opacity to zero to make it invisible. - Save the project file after dummy application. --- ## Aligning the Shoe with Clo Avatar and Registering as an Accessory This section covers aligning the finished shoe to the Clo avatar and registering it as an accessory file (.zax). - Clear workspace; open Clo female avatar. - Remove default heel shoes from avatar. - Import your saved shoe project. - Positions may not match initially; adjust during registration. - To register: 1. Select all shoe patterns. 2. Right-click in 3D window → Convert → Avatar Accessory. 3. Set Accessory Type to **Shoes and Flats**. 4. Select **Patterns** under Object; verify all pieces are present. 5. Use gizmo to adjust shoe position relative to avatar. 6. Check **Mirror Creation** to auto-generate opposite foot shoe. 7. Click Save. - Load the saved .zax accessory file on the Clo avatar. - Avatar switches to heel-down pose with shoes applied. - Shoes move naturally with avatar during pose or motion changes. --- ## Working with Heel Outsoles This section explains applying heel-style outsoles, including scaling and glue attachment. - Heel outsoles are only available as trim files; no insole pattern required. - Load the saved shoe last project with only the upper visible. - Drag and drop heel outsole trim into the 3D window; defaults to left foot. - Use the Move tool and gizmo to position outsole. - To scale heel height: 1. Select outsole trim in Object Browser → Trim tab. 2. In Property Editor, uncheck **Lock Aspect Ratio**. 3. Adjust Y-axis scale value (e.g., 90 mm) to stretch heel vertically. - Attach heel outsole to insole using Glue (bottom view, select outsole bottom surface, activate Glue mode, hover and click insole pattern). - Fine-tune position with gizmo. - Create dummy and save final shoe as .zax file following sneaker workflow. --- ## Applying Heel Drop Outsoles with Sloped Bottoms This section details the specialized approach for heel drop outsoles, which have uneven, sloped bottoms thicker at the heel. - Heel drop outsoles require creating the outsole pattern directly from the outsole file instead of from the shoe last, due to the unique heel slope. - Process: 1. Purchase and download the Chunky Boots outsole from Connect. 2. Extract the zip file containing: - Shoe outsole trim file. - Project file with 3D pen line on outsole OBJ as an avatar. 3. Load the avatar file with 3D pen line. 4. Use **Flatten tool** to select the 3D pen line area and generate outsole pattern. 5. Set particle distance to 5 and collision thickness to 1 for the pattern. 6. Position and freeze the outsole pattern with the gizmo. - Load your shoe last project and apply the heel drop outsole: - Delete sole pattern from upper. - Reposition shoe last and upper to avoid intersection with outsole. - Delete the imported outsole avatar file used for extraction. - Sew flattened outsole pattern to the upper pattern correctly. - Select all upper patterns, apply **Strengthen** to prevent distortion. - Run simulation to fit upper to outsole shape. - Import outsole trim and glue it to the upper pattern. - Create dummy pattern for stable simulation. - Save final shoe as a .zax file. --- ## Important Notes on Heel Drop Outsole Positioning and Registration - Heel drop outsoles must be positioned correctly to align with the foot. - If the outsole is off the outer rim or not aligned, the shoe will not register properly. - Load the saved shoe accessory and apply it to the avatar to verify correct fit and appearance. --- ## Conclusion This guide demonstrated how to use Clo’s new shoe outsole assets for creating sneakers, heels, and heel drop shoes. By following the outlined procedures for downloading, attaching, gluing, simulating, and registering, users can create realistic, fully functional shoe accessories compatible with Clo avatars. The provided files enable a variety of custom footwear designs with accurate structural and visual details.

Position and freeze the outsole pattern with the gizmo. - Load your shoe last project and apply the heel drop outsole: - Delete sole pattern from upper. - Reposition shoe last and upper to avoid intersection with outsole. - Delete the imported outsole avatar file used for extraction. - Sew flattened outsole pattern to the upper pattern correctly. - Select all upper patterns, apply **Strengthen** to prevent distortion. - Run simulation to fit upper to outsole shape. - Import outsole trim and glue it to the upper pattern. - Create dummy pattern for stable simulation. - Save final shoe as a .zax file. --- ## Important Notes on Heel Drop Outsole Positioning and Registration - Heel drop outsoles must be positioned correctly to align with the foot. - If the outsole is off the outer rim or not aligned, the shoe will not register properly. - Load the saved shoe accessory and apply it to the avatar to verify correct fit and appearance. --- ## Conclusion This guide demonstrated how to use Clo’s new shoe outsole assets for creating sneakers, heels, and heel drop shoes. By following the outlined procedures for downloading, attaching, gluing, simulating, and registering, users can create realistic, fully functional shoe accessories compatible with Clo avatars.
